findings.title: packages/runtime/README.md's --print-closure example prints the wrong denominator (312 entries; the real count is 299)
findings.evidence: The README block added by f01b4d34 shows '# freeze-lint closure report - module "packages/runtime/lib/work-trace.mjs" is locked by 6 of / # 312 @frozen entry file(s):'. The real command prints '6 of 299 @frozen entry file(s)'. 312 is the number of frozen MODULES (the manifest's workflows count), not the number of @frozen ENTRY files (299). The lane's final report repeats the conflation for #849 ('none of the other 306'); the true figure is 293 other entries.
findings.required_fix: Correct the README example to '6 of 299 @frozen entry file(s)' (or elide the counts), and correct the same line in the lane report.

findings.title: --retire with no path argument silently falls through to an ordinary verify and exits 0
findings.evidence: Reviewer ran 'node scripts/check-frozen-workflows.mjs --retire' in the worktree: it printed 'freeze-lint: OK - 312 frozen file(s) verified ... 3 retired entr(ies) recorded.' and exited 0. RETIRE_PATH is process.argv[RETIRE_INDEX + 1] ?? null and the retire block is guarded by 'if (RETIRE_PATH)', so a mistyped or truncated retire reports success with no hint the command was ignored. Every other refusal in this command is loud and fail-closed, which makes this one inconsistent with its own design.
findings.required_fix: Refuse when --retire is present with no path (exit 1, usage message), in the same fail-closed shape the other three refusals already use.

findings.title: The '#849 REAL repo canary' cell would pass against a filter that is a complete no-op
findings.evidence: scripts/check-frozen-workflows.selftest.mjs: the cell named '#849 REAL repo canary: filtering the real closure to lib/work-trace.mjs matches the #815 unfiltered attribution exactly' only iterates reachedBy(module) asserting each expected entry appears in the filtered report. It never asserts the other 293 entries are absent, so an implementation of formatClosureReport(closure, filter) that ignored the filter and returned the full report would still pass it - the opposite of what its name claims. The exclusion direction is proven only by the synthetic cell above it.
findings.required_fix: Add the exclusion half to that cell (assert at least one non-reaching real entry is absent from the filtered report), or rename it so it no longer claims 'exactly'.

findings.title: No cell proves redo refuses on a non-rig (non-ephemeral) target, which the lane brief named explicitly
findings.evidence: The lane brief states 'the redo mode must be gated behind the destructive flag and refuse on a non-rig target'. packages/db/tests/migrate-redo.test.mjs AC2 covers only the first half: it deletes CLARA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE and asserts /destructive|CLARA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE/i. Every cell in the file connects to 127.0.0.1, which targetIsEphemeral() accepts, so the second limb of assertDestructiveAllowed (packages/db/lib/guard.mjs:81-86, 'REFUSED for non-ephemeral target ... set CLARA_DESTRUCTIVE_TARGET="user@host:port/db"') is never reached on the redo path. The behaviour is correct by delegation - migrate.mjs calls the shared gate before opening any connection, reviewer read-verified - but the brief's named requirement is unproven for redo.
findings.required_fix: Add one connection-free cell: CLARA_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=1, PGHOST at a non-ephemeral label, CLARA_DESTRUCTIVE_TARGET unset, redo set -> rejects with /REFUSED for non-ephemeral target/, with a clientFactory that throws to prove no connection opens.

The AC's literal command ends in 'node scripts/backup.mjs --profile full', which neither the lane nor I ran (it needs a hosted DSN and pg_dump 17). Reviewer read-verified the remaining link: backup.mjs -> childEnvForExternalTools() -> resolveTarget() (packages/db/lib/pg.mjs:57-69) falls back to the PG* vars when DATABASE_URL is absent, and PGSSLMODE/PGSSLROOTCERT are both in WSL_ENV_LIST.
findings.required_fix: None before merge. Record in the release runbook that the first ceremony using --child-os wsl is the AC1 proof, and capture that transcript.

findings.title: Case-count mismatch: the report and commit message say 11 new (#917) cells; the run prints 10

findings.title: cn is dropped AFTER the pinned CLI writes it, not before, leaving a window and lockfile churn the ticket's Desired behaviour set out to remove
findings.evidence: apps/web/scripts/ui-add.mjs main(): 'const code = spawnAdd(argv); ... stripLocalDependencies(local)' -> defaultStripLocalDependencies runs 'pnpm remove cn'. The ticket's Desired behaviour offers two shapes, 'Either the guard drops it before the CLI writes it, or it refuses and names it'; this is a third. The AC ('leaves no cn entry ... with no manual revert') is met, but between spawnAdd and the strip, package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml do carry cn - an interrupt there leaves exactly the hand-revert the ticket exists to abolish - and every such install now writes the lockfile twice. The lane's own rehearsal recorded incidental peer-annotation churn (a debug variant gaining/losing supports-color) from the add-then-remove cycle.
findings.required_fix: Record the ordering choice and its window explicitly in apps/web/components/ui/README.md (which currently reads as if nothing is ever written), or file a follow-up to pre-filter the dependency before the CLI's install step.

findings.title: defaultStripLocalDependencies (the real 'pnpm remove' edge) has no committed cell
findings.evidence: Every #969 cell injects stripLocalDependencies through main()'s deps object; the real implementation is exercised only by the live rehearsal recorded in the lane report. This follows the file's own stated convention for defaultSpawnAdd/defaultResolveFiles, so it is house-consistent. The untested failure mode worth knowing: 'pnpm remove <name>' on a dependency that is not present exits non-zero (ERR_PNPM_CANNOT_REMOVE_MISSING_DEPS), and main() would then propagate that as the whole ui:add's exit code after an otherwise successful install.
findings.required_fix: None required. Optionally note the missing-dependency exit path in the guard's own header.

findings.title: The whole-tree equivalence holds at the verdict level, but the change does move internal classification data on 6 migrations - not mentioned in the report
findings.evidence: Reviewer built an old-vs-new harness (pre-fix module from dd3f8f1d vs HEAD) over all 229 files in packages/db/migrations. scanSources is byte-identical (0 findings both sides; scanned {functions:1410, patches:212} both sides), and maskComments, parseFunctions, dynamicSqlFindings and executeExpressions are identical on EVERY file. parseCoRPatches differs on 6 files (0119_f_a3_pr1a_core_extractions, 0129_f_a3_pr3_retirement_parity_doors, 0134_f_a3_pr3_c1bis_receipt_identity, 0136_fix_freeform_basis_types, 0226_bank_match_evidence, 0234_legal_enforcement_mode) and quotedLiterals on 119 - but the movement is confined to the 'fragments' array; line, tag, kind, targets, censusOnly, censusReads and whitelisted are unchanged on every patch. AC5 therefore holds, and the change is if anything strictly more fail-closed (content previously swallowed to EOF is now scanned). The report's flat 'identical before and after' is true of the CLI verdict and understates the actual blast radius.
findings.required_fix: Add one sentence to the lane report recording the measured blast radius (fragments only; classification fields unchanged on all 229 files), so a future author knows what this change can and cannot move.

findings.title: The whole apps/web suite is flaky at this size: one of two reviewer runs had 1 failure
findings.evidence: node scripts/run-tests.mjs from apps/web, run 1: '# tests 4633 / # pass 4630 / # fail 1 / # skipped 2'. Run 2 on the same tree: '# tests 4633 / # pass 4631 / # fail 0 / # skipped 2', exactly matching the lane report. The failing test's identity was not captured (run 1's stream was tail-truncated). RIG.md names a known whole-suite load flake in thread-live-clarify.test.tsx that this lane did not touch. The lane's '0 fail' claim is reproducible but is a one-run observation, not a stable property.
findings.required_fix: None for this lane. The orchestrator should not read a single green whole-suite run as proof, and should re-run before attributing a failure.

findings.title: TDD slicing cannot be read off the branch: each ticket is one commit carrying its tests and its implementation together
findings.evidence: git log origin/main..HEAD shows exactly six commits, one per ticket, each adding 5-11 new cells plus the implementation, so the red -> green per slice that work-order rule 4 requires is not visible in history. The cells themselves are non-vacuous: reviewer proved red-before independently for #959 (ran the pre-fix module - dollar-tag and quote masking both false, censusOnly [false] / censusReads [] versus [true] / [{v_n}] after), and every other ticket's new cells import symbols that do not exist at the merge-base (retireFrozenEntry, toWslPath/resolveChildOs, classifyDependencies, the redo option, the reworded message). Only the ORDER rests on the lane report's word.
findings.required_fix: None. Noted so the orchestrator knows which half of rule 4 the branch evidences and which half is self-reported.

findings.title: The branch is one merge behind origin/main, so 'git diff origin/main..HEAD' misreports four deletions that are not this lane's work
findings.evidence: merge-base = dd3f8f1d; origin/main = e7f0a10a (which landed docs/PROGRESS.md changes, RELEASE-AS-RUN.md, ceremony/reads-0234.mjs and GRILL-2026-09-20.md). 'git diff --stat origin/main..HEAD' shows those as deletions plus a 43-line PROGRESS.md change; 'git diff --stat dd3f8f1d..HEAD' shows the lane's true 20 files, 1383 insertions, 46 deletions. Nothing in the lane touches any of those four paths ('git log origin/main..HEAD -- <path>' is empty for each).
findings.required_fix: Review and integrate against the merge-base; rebase or merge main before the integration PR so the diff reads honestly.
